verses.text: When Saul's son Ishbosheth heard that Abner had died in Hebron, he lost all courage, and all the Israelites were afraid.

Saul's son had two men who were leaders of raiding groups. One was named Baanah and the other Rechab. They were sons of Rimmon from Beeroth, from the tribe of Benjamin. Beeroth was counted as part of Benjamin,
because the people of Beeroth had run away to Gittaim, and they have lived there as foreigners to this day.

Saul's son Jonathan had a son who was crippled in both feet. He was five years old when the news about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse picked him up and ran, but as she hurried away, he fell and became crippled. His name was Mephibosheth.
Rechab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmon from Beeroth, set out and came to Ishbosheth's house in the heat of the day, while he was resting at noon.
They went into the house as if to get some wheat, and they stabbed him in the stomach. Then Rechab and his brother Baanah escaped.

They had come into the house while he was lying on his bed in his bedroom. They stabbed him and killed him, and cut off his head. They took his head and travelled all night along the road through the Arabah valley.

They brought Ishbosheth's head to David at Hebron and said to the king, "Here is the head of Ishbosheth, son of Saul, your enemy who tried to kill you! Today the LORD has paid back Saul and his family for you, my lord the king."
David answered Rechab and his brother Baanah, the sons of Rimmon from Beeroth: "As surely as the LORD lives, who has rescued me from every trouble,
when a man told me, 'Saul is dead,' he thought he was bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him in Ziklag. That was the reward I gave him for his news.
How much more must I now punish wicked men who have killed an innocent man on his own bed in his own house! Shouldn't I make you pay for his blood and wipe you off the earth?"

So David gave orders to his young men, and they killed them. They cut off their hands and feet and hung their bodies beside the pool in Hebron. But they took Ishbosheth's head and buried it in Abner's grave in Hebron.
